#!/bin/bash
# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables (unquoted slot),
# then reference them only as "$VAR" - never interpolate 
# inside a quoted context. See kubernetes_jq_query for the rationale.
KIND=pods
CUSTOM_COLUMNS='NAME:.metadata.name,READY:.status.containerStatuses[*].ready,STATUS:.status.phase,NODE:.spec.nodeName,IP:.status.podIP,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount,START:.status.startTime'
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
FILTER_PATTERN=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""
[ "$FILTER_PATTERN" = "None" ] && FILTER_PATTERN=""

# kubectl ignores -n for cluster-scoped kinds; say so instead of reporting a namespace that wasn't applied
NOTES='[]'
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  is_kind() { awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind || index($1, kind ".") == 1 {found = 1} END {exit !found}'; }
  if kubectl api-resources --namespaced=false -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind \
    && ! kubectl api-resources --namespaced=true -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind; then
    NOTES=$(jq -nc --arg note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${KIND} is cluster-scoped." '[$note]')
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
fi

SCOPE_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-n "$SEL_NAMESPACE")
else
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--all-namespaces)
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-l "$SEL_LABELS")
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--field-selector "$SEL_FIELDS")
fi

err_file=$(mktemp)
output=$(kubectl get "$KIND" "${SCOPE_ARGS[@]}" -o custom-columns="$CUSTOM_COLUMNS" 2>"$err_file")
kubectl_exit=$?
err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

SCOPE='null'
if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
    '{namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
      label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
      field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')
fi

if [ $kubectl_exit -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$output" ]; then
  if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
    jq -n --arg stderr "$err_content" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
      '{count: 0, header: null, rows: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  else
    echo "=== STDERR ==="
    echo "$err_content"
    echo "=== ROWS ==="
    echo "=== COUNT ==="
    echo 0
  fi
  exit 0
fi

# Split header and data rows
header=$(echo "$output" | head -1)
if [ -n "$FILTER_PATTERN" ]; then
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2 | grep -E -- "$FILTER_PATTERN" || true)
else
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2)
fi

if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then
    count=$(echo "$data" | wc -l)
  else
    count=0
  fi
  # Rows go through stdin, not --argjson, so large tables don't hit "Argument list too long"
  printf '%s' "$data" | jq -R . | jq -s \
    --argjson count "$count" \
    --arg header "$header" \
    --arg stderr "$err_content" \
    --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
    '{count: $count, header: $header, rows: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
else
  echo "=== STDERR ==="
  echo "$err_content"
  echo "=== HEADER ==="
  echo "$header"
  echo "=== ROWS ==="
  echo "$data"
  echo "=== COUNT ==="
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then echo "$data" | wc -l; else echo 0; fi
fi

#!/bin/bash

# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=services
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, type: .spec.type, clusterIP: .spec.clusterIP, ports: [.spec.ports[] | {name, port, targetPort, protocol}], selector: .spec.selector, labels: .metadata.labels}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

    && ! kubectl api-resources --namespaced=true -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind; then
    NOTES=$(jq -nc --arg note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${KIND} is cluster-scoped." '[$note]')
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
fi

SCOPE_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-n "$SEL_NAMESPACE")
else
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--all-namespaces)
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-l "$SEL_LABELS")
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--field-selector "$SEL_FIELDS")
fi

err_file=$(mktemp)
output=$(kubectl get "$KIND" "${SCOPE_ARGS[@]}" -o custom-columns="$CUSTOM_COLUMNS" 2>"$err_file")
kubectl_exit=$?
err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

SCOPE='null'
if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
    '{namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
      label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
      field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')
fi

if [ $kubectl_exit -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$output" ]; then
  if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
    jq -n --arg stderr "$err_content" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
      '{count: 0, header: null, rows: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  else
    echo "=== STDERR ==="
    echo "$err_content"
    echo "=== ROWS ==="
    echo "=== COUNT ==="
    echo 0
  fi
  exit 0
fi

# Split header and data rows
header=$(echo "$output" | head -1)
if [ -n "$FILTER_PATTERN" ]; then
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2 | grep -E -- "$FILTER_PATTERN" || true)
else
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2)
fi

if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then
    count=$(echo "$data" | wc -l)
  else
    count=0
  fi
  # Rows go through stdin, not --argjson, so large tables don't hit "Argument list too long"
  printf '%s' "$data" | jq -R . | jq -s \
    --argjson count "$count" \
    --arg header "$header" \
    --arg stderr "$err_content" \
    --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
    '{count: $count, header: $header, rows: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
else
  echo "=== STDERR ==="
  echo "$err_content"
  echo "=== HEADER ==="
  echo "$header"
  echo "=== ROWS ==="
  echo "$data"
  echo "=== COUNT ==="
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then echo "$data" | wc -l; else echo 0; fi
fi

#!/bin/bash
# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables (unquoted slot),
# then reference them only as "$VAR" - never interpolate 
# inside a quoted context. See kubernetes_jq_query for the rationale.
KIND=replicasets
CUSTOM_COLUMNS='NAME:.metadata.name,REPLICAS:.spec.replicas,IMAGE:.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image,OWNER:.metadata.ownerReferences[0].name'
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
FILTER_PATTERN=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""
[ "$FILTER_PATTERN" = "None" ] && FILTER_PATTERN=""

# kubectl ignores -n for cluster-scoped kinds; say so instead of reporting a namespace that wasn't applied
NOTES='[]'
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  is_kind() { awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind || index($1, kind ".") == 1 {found = 1} END {exit !found}'; }
  if kubectl api-resources --namespaced=false -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind \
    && ! kubectl api-resources --namespaced=true -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind; then
    NOTES=$(jq -nc --arg note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${KIND} is cluster-scoped." '[$note]')
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
fi

SCOPE_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-n "$SEL_NAMESPACE")
else
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--all-namespaces)
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-l "$SEL_LABELS")
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--field-selector "$SEL_FIELDS")
fi

err_file=$(mktemp)
output=$(kubectl get "$KIND" "${SCOPE_ARGS[@]}" -o custom-columns="$CUSTOM_COLUMNS" 2>"$err_file")
kubectl_exit=$?
err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

SCOPE='null'
if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
    '{namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
      label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
      field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')
fi

if [ $kubectl_exit -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$output" ]; then
  if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
    jq -n --arg stderr "$err_content" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
      '{count: 0, header: null, rows: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  else
    echo "=== STDERR ==="
    echo "$err_content"
    echo "=== ROWS ==="
    echo "=== COUNT ==="
    echo 0
  fi
  exit 0
fi

# Split header and data rows
header=$(echo "$output" | head -1)
if [ -n "$FILTER_PATTERN" ]; then
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2 | grep -E -- "$FILTER_PATTERN" || true)
else
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2)
fi

if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then
    count=$(echo "$data" | wc -l)
  else
    count=0
  fi
  # Rows go through stdin, not --argjson, so large tables don't hit "Argument list too long"
  printf '%s' "$data" | jq -R . | jq -s \
    --argjson count "$count" \
    --arg header "$header" \
    --arg stderr "$err_content" \
    --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
    '{count: $count, header: $header, rows: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
else
  echo "=== STDERR ==="
  echo "$err_content"
  echo "=== HEADER ==="
  echo "$header"
  echo "=== ROWS ==="
  echo "$data"
  echo "=== COUNT ==="
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then echo "$data" | wc -l; else echo 0; fi
fi

#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=services
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, applied: (.metadata.annotations["kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration"] // "<none>" | fromjson? | {ports: .spec.ports, selector: .spec.selector}), live: {ports: .spec.ports, selector: .spec.selector}}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

## 结论

第 2 轮的**方向是对的**（约 200ms 的固定档位、零错误、各服务自身都是毫秒级），但**范围说错了**：这不是"整条链路上随机丢一个报文"，而是**逐次 RPC 命中**，而且本次找到了一个**跨 pod、应用无关的硬证据**——kubelet 自己的探针连 productcatalogservice 的 Pod IP 都连不上（>1s）；这排除了应用逻辑，把矛头指向**单节点 kind 集群的 Pod 网络/内核数据面**。仓库内已没有任何可调的配置错误。

## 哪些被证实、哪些被推翻

**被证实：**
1. **约 205ms 的固定档位**：前端的 `took_ms` 只出现 8–15ms、214/215/216/217/219/221/223、385/421/424/434/437/495、648 这些数值——正好是 +1、+2、+3 个 ~205ms 单元。205ms ≈ Linux `TCP_RTO_MIN`（丢一个报文→200ms 后重传）。
2. **各服务自身处理都是微秒～毫秒级**（15 分钟窗口实测）：
   - shippingservice `[GetQuote] received` → `completed` 相差 **0.04ms**（18:53:51.674806→.674845）；
   - currencyservice 每个 `conversion request successful` 都在 1–2ms 内；
   - redis-cart 健康：`BGSAVE` 每 300s 一次（18:41:15 / 18:46:16 / 18:51:17），10 个 key，`BGSAVE done` 约 10ms、`terminated with success` 约 100ms，无 slowlog；
   - cartservice 逐条打印 `GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync`，无任何异常、无线程池告警（888 行/20 分钟）。
3. **零错误**：45 分钟内 frontend 只有 18:46 我们自己 rollout 期间的 17 条 warning/error（`connection refused`、`i/o timeout`、`context deadline`），业务期没有任何 5xx 或 RPC 报错。
4. **kubelet 探针（绕过 Service、直连 Pod IP）也超时**——这是最关键的新证据：
   - `productcatalogservice-7457c7c77f-qxtdw`（10.244.0.108:3550）：`Liveness probe failed: timeout: failed to connect service ... within 1s` **9 次**、`Readiness probe failed` **9 次**，持续到 18:44:55/18:44:57；
   - 换新 Pod 后 `productcatalogservice-6847445d46-nfcdl`（10.244.0.116:3550）在 **18:48:05** 又失败 1 次；
   - 该 Pod 整个生命周期只有 5 行日志（`starting grpc server`、`successfully parsed product catalog json` 等），**进程完全空闲**却连 1 秒内建连都做不到。其余 11 个服务的探针失败只发生在容器刚启动的那一刻（`initialDelay` 内），不属于这一类。

**被推翻：**
1. **第 1 轮 CPU 限流**：8 个 Deployment 的 CPU 上限放宽 8–10 倍（125m/200m/300m → 1 核）后，用户侧 21.0% → 22.6% → 19.6%，p90 219→220→220，p99 431→435→496，**完全没动**。CPU 不是原因。
2. **cartservice/redis 连接状态**：第 2 轮重启 cartservice 无改善；redis 无背压、无大 key、BGSAVE 正常。
3. **配置错误（第 2 轮未排除的部分，现已排除）**：12 个 Service 的 live spec 与 `last-applied-configuration` **逐字段一致**（含 emailservice 5000→8080、frontend 80→8080），12 个 Endpoints 各自精确指向自己的那一个 Pod；命名空间内除 `kube-root-ca.crt` 外**没有任何 ConfigMap**，没有配额/LimitRange；20 个 ReplicaSet 全部是 v0.10.3，无残留旧版本 Pod。→ **不是 targetPort/selector/env 注入类故障**。

**新发现（第 2 轮没看到的规律）：慢请求概率与"页面串行 RPC 跳数"成正比**
前端自身 `took_ms ≥ 100ms` 的比例（15 分钟、共 2217 个请求）：`GET /` **7.5%**(17/227) < `GET /cart`+`POST /cart` **23%**(181/788) < `GET /product/*` **28%**(315/1110) < `POST /cart/checkout` **35%**(32/92)，整体 24%，与用户侧 21% 一致。首页只用 `ListProducts`（不调单条 `GetProduct`），而 /product、/cart、checkout 都会调**单条 GetProduct**——这与"最活跃的异常点是 productcatalogservice 的端点"相互印证（注意：这是相关性，未能用 trace 进一步证实）。

**仍未解释的现象：**
- 首页 7.5% 与其余 23–35% 的差异，说明惩罚不是"按时间"均匀施加的全局冻结，而是附在具体 RPC 上；
- 18:53:54 前后 currencyservice 日志出现**成批到达**（.188 两个 `Getting supported currencies`、.190 两次转换；随后 .404、.410/.411/.412），即前端页面以 ~205–215ms 为节拍成批释放——这与"丢包 → 200ms 重传 → HTTP/2 队头阻塞释放同连接上所有并发 RPC"吻合；
- 为什么探针超时**只出现在 productcatalogservice**（两代 Pod 都出现，说明不是单个 Pod 状态问题），以及节点侧 veth/cni0/conntrack 的实际丢包计数——**本账号无权查看**：`nodes is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:diag-system:diag-agent" cannot list resource "nodes"`，kube-system 亦不可读。

## 为什么这一轮不提修复动作

可用的 6 个操作全部作用在 boutique 的 Deployment/Service 上（restart / set_env / unset_env / scale / set_cpu_limit / set_service_selector / set_service_target_port）。这一轮已经证明：
- 配置层面（selector、targetPort、env、镜像、副本）**全部正确**，改了只会制造错误；
- CPU 上限已放宽到 1 核仍无变化，再调无意义；
- 两代 productcatalog Pod 都出现端点不可达 → 不是单个 Pod 的病态状态，`restart` 也解决不了（且 rollout 期间会像 18:46 那样产生 500 和 18s 级长尾，反而污染指标）。

真正要动的是**节点**，不属于本账号权限，需要运维直接处理。

## 请运维在节点 `tiktok-k8s-lab-control-plane` 上执行（按优先级）

1. 确认丢包/重传：`netstat -s | egrep -i 'retransmit|listen (overflows|drops)'`、`nstat -az | egrep 'TcpExtTCPTimeouts|TcpExtListenDrops|TcpExtTCPReqQFullDrop|TcpRetransSegs'`，持续采样 60s（应看到随慢请求同步增长）。
2. conntrack：`cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` 与 `..._max`，`dmesg | grep -i 'nf_conntrack: table full'`。
3. 网卡/队列丢包：`ip -s link show cni0`、逐个 `veth*`（`ip -s link show | grep -A2 veth`），`tc -s qdisc show dev cni0`、`ethtool -S` 看 `tx_dropped`/`no_space`；`net.core.netdev_max_backlog`、`net.core.somaxconn` 是否被压满。
4. 单节点 kind 的"控制面与负载争抢"：`etcdctl endpoint status --write-out=table`（WAL fsync 是否出现 ~200ms 抖动）、`iostat -x 1`、`vmstat 1`（`wa`/`r` 队列）、`pidstat -w 1 | grep -E 'kubelet|containerd|etcd|kube-apiserver'`。
5. 判定后修复：把 boutique 迁到独立节点/多节点集群，或 `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=...`、调 `net.core.netdev_max_backlog`，并重装/升级 kindnet；若 etcd/磁盘是瓶颈，隔离控制面 I/O。

如果运维希望仍只用集群内手段做**对照实验**：把 boutique 整体迁移到另一节点（新集群）后如果 21% 立刻归零，即可确认节点数据面为根因。

# Investigation guidelines

* Gather data with as many tool calls as needed before responding; keep going until you reach the deepest root cause you can find.
* Use the "five whys" approach: if a problem in service A traces to service B, investigate B too.
* Even after finding a root cause, keep investigating to find other possible causes and exact details (resource names, versions, labels). If there are multiple possible causes, list them in a numbered list.
* Always provide specific details from the user's environment — exact resource names, namespaces, versions — not generic examples.
* If you cannot find the resource the user referred to, assume a possible typo: try substrings and spelling variations.
* **Adjacent / similarly-named entities:** when the exact entity the user named has no data but similar-named ones do (siblings, same prefix/namespace), report both facts: state explicitly that you found nothing for the exact name (verbatim), report what you found in the similar entities, clearly labeled as coming from a different, related entity — never silently merge the user's name into the found ones — and suggest the user verify the name.
* Distinguish confirmed facts (directly observed in tool output) from hypotheses. Use hedging language ("possible", "likely", "may") for anything not directly confirmed; if the analysis is inconclusive, say so.
* Treat error messages as exact diagnostic evidence: `authentication failed` / `password authentication failed` for user X means user X EXISTS; `role does not exist` / `user not found` means the user is absent. These are mutually exclusive — never add "or the user may not exist" to an authentication failure.
* Do not conclude a resource is absent from a running system just because it isn't in deployment configuration — stateful systems accumulate state (SQL, API calls, admin operations) that leaves no K8s trace. If you can't read a value (e.g. a Secret), say you couldn't verify it rather than guessing.
* Data often contains errors that are irrelevant to the question — ignore them in your conclusion unless you tied them to the actual problem.
* ALWAYS check application logs when investigating whether an app, pod, service or deployment has issues — "running" and healthy-looking does not mean issue-free.

# Impact and blast radius

* Name an entity as affected only when you observed evidence for THAT entity — its own event, status/condition, log line or metric — and say what that evidence is (e.g. "`checkout-cache`: Evicted event, now Pending").
* Never widen the blast radius by inference. A node condition does not tell you which pods it hit; a failing dependency does not tell you which of its clients broke; an unhealthy shared component does not mean its consumers are unhealthy. Check each entity before you name it, or do not name it — sampling a workload's replicas characterizes the WORKLOAD, so attribute what you found to it rather than to replicas you did not look at.
* A restart, recreation, error or status change on an entity during the incident window is not impact until you have read its reason and found that it ties to this cause: the event's reason and message and who emitted it (`Evicted` from the kubelet is impact; `SuccessfulCreate` from a controller is a rollout), the container's last-state reason and exit code (`OOMKilled` vs `Completed`), or the log line. A pod that is 5 minutes old on a node that had trouble 5 minutes ago was not necessarily evicted — check what created it. Coincidence in time is not causation, and "also affected" is a claim that needs its own evidence.
* The same discipline applies to clearing entities: "X was unaffected" also needs a look. If you did not check, say you did not check.
* Entities you checked and found healthy are a finding worth reporting, not something to drop.
* Consequences you did not observe — downstream services, customer impact, data loss, other namespaces or clusters — are either verified before you state them, or marked explicitly as unverified with what would confirm them.
* Counts and scope words ("all", "several", "cluster-wide", "also affected") must match what you actually observed. Do not generalize from a sample you did not take.
* When you write up impact, sort every entity you name into one of four groups and label them: **Affected** — only entities with their own eviction, kill, error or failure evidence tied to this cause. Every line here quotes the exact reason token that proves it, in parentheses: `Evicted`, `OOMKilled`, `BackOff`, `Failed`, `Unhealthy` on a long-running pod, an error log line. If you cannot quote such a token for that entity, it does not go here — `SuccessfulDelete`, `SuccessfulCreate`, `Scheduled`, `Started` and a probe miss at startup are not among them. A recreation, restart or probe miss inside the window is never enough on its own, whatever sub-label you give it; **Checked, healthy** — you looked and found nothing wrong; **Changed during the window for another reason** — it restarted, was recreated or errored, and you name what did it (a controller rollout, a scheduled job, an operator, a probe at startup) and how you know; **Not checked**. Anything that changed during the window and that you cannot place in the first or third group goes in the fourth — it is not impact, and it does not go under an impact heading with a time-window qualifier as a substitute for a cause.

# If investigating Kubernetes problems

* Run as many kubectl commands as needed, walking the ownership chain (e.g. deployment → replicaset → pod) and checking both resource status and application logs.
* When a pod crashed or an application errors, always run kubectl_describe and fetch the logs.
* Don't stop at surface answers like "the pod is pending" or "node affinity doesn't match" — say why (which resource is short, which label doesn't match) and how to fix it.
* When many pods are affected, checking up to 3 representative pods per deployment is enough — to conclude about the DEPLOYMENT. Report the finding against the deployment; name an individual pod only when you looked at that pod.
* Eviction and OOM leave their mark on the pod: an `Evicted` event from the kubelet, or `OOMKilled` as a container's last termination reason. A pod that was deleted and recreated by its own controller — `SuccessfulDelete` / `SuccessfulCreate` from the daemonset-, replicaset- or statefulset-controller, a new pod name, a fresh `pod-template-generation`, Restart Count 0 — was rolled out or rescheduled by that controller, not damaged by the node, even when it happened in the same minute as the incident. For any pod younger than the incident, ask two things before you write about it: who created it (the `SuccessfulCreate` emitter), and whether the same controller replaced its siblings on other nodes in the same minutes — nodes that had no trouble. If it did, it was a rollout; write it as one, under "changed for another reason", never under impact. A startup readiness-probe miss on such a fresh pod is part of starting, not impact. Count a pod as affected only on its own eviction or kill evidence.
* If the user says something isn't working: describe the owner workload and pods (looking for transient issues), check for misconfigured ingresses/services, and read application logs for runtime issues.

Count: page at .188 had 2 getCurrencies? Two pages started at the same ms (.188 ×2) → 2 pages. Conversions at .190 ×2. Then a page at .404 with conversions at .410, .411, .412 (4 conversions = one page with 4 prices?)

Interesting: the sequences show "Getting supported currencies" immediately followed by conversions within 2-7ms.

Now let me count: 3514 log lines in 5 min = 11.7/s. That's a LOT. Pages are ~2/s. So ~6 currency log lines per page.

Hmm, so total currency RPC count ≈ 2400/300s = 8/s (conversions + getCurrencies). That's high; ~4 conversions per page on average.

Something notable: is there a pattern of a long gap before a burst? Let me look for gaps. In this sample: .964, .188 (224ms later!), .404 (216ms!), .692 (288ms). 

WOW: 18:53:53.964 → 18:53:54.188 = 224ms gap; .188 → .404 = 216ms; .404 → .692 = 288ms. These gaps are ~200-288ms and match the "step" pattern! But gaps in a 11.7/s event stream of 224ms are just traffic randomness? At 11.7/s, a 224ms gap has probability ~e^(-2.6)=7%. Three in a row is unlikely.

Hmm! But wait — these are "latest 15 of 2416" — sorted oldest→newest? They go .964, .964, .964(4 conversions), then .188, .188, .190, .190, .404, .410, .410, .411, .412, .692, .694. That's 15 lines in chronological order. So we see 4 conversions at .964, then a 224ms gap, then 2 getCurrencies at .188 + 2 conversions at .190, then 216ms gap, then getCurrencies at .404 + 4 conversions at .410-.412, then 280ms gap, then getCurrencies at .692 + conversion at .694.

This is the pattern of pages arriving in "waves" every ~220ms! Each wave = a couple of pages. That means the frontend is processing pages in bursts every ~200-220ms — consistent with the HOL/quantized-stall model: the frontend's requests are being released in batches.

Hmm, and note: 2 pages starting at the exact same ms (.188, .188) — synchronized releases again!

So the system has a periodic ~210ms cycle where requests get released in groups. Hmm, that's not just "20% of requests +200ms"; it's a global quantization of ~210ms for a subset.

Anyway, I'm now quite confident this is a systemic stall cycle of ~200-215ms affecting the frontend and its RPCs. It occurs ~1-2 times per second.

What creates a ~210ms global cycle? Candidates: 
- CFS throttling (100ms period) — 2 periods = 200ms. Fits! If a container bursts and gets throttled for 2 quota periods... but we raised limits to 1 core for 8 services.
- WHICH container still has a tight limit? loadgenerator: 500m limit, 300m request! And emailservice 200m, shippingservice 200m, paymentservice 200m. And **the loadgenerator (locust, Python) with 500m limit**! If locust gets throttled, it doesn't affect frontend latency though (frontend measures internally).

WAIT. WAIT. What about the container that measures: the metric "user-side" comes from... the load generator? "最近 45 秒前端处理了 167 个请求" — "前端处理了167个请求" = the frontend handled 167 requests. And the latency percentiles match the frontend's own took_ms (median 10ms, p90 219). So it's the frontend's view.

Now: which container in the *frontend's request path* still has a 200m limit? emailservice (200m), paymentservice (200m), shippingservice (200m), loadgenerator (500m). Shippingservice is on the cart/checkout path only. Not home/product.

Hmm, so CFS throttling of email/payment/shipping can't explain product page.

BUT: our probes showed productcatalogservice's pod unreachable. Also, notably, productcatalogservice had CPU limit 200m before round 2 (raised at 18:46). And the probe failures at 18:44:55 were BEFORE the raise (200m). The one at 18:48:05 was AFTER (1 core). So CFS throttling of productcatalog can't explain 18:48:05.

Hmm OK.

What about the **kubelet** doing something every N ms? No.

What about the **node's network stack** with `net.core.netdev_max_backlog` etc? 

Honestly, the ~210ms wave cycle with 4 conversions in the same ms strongly smells like **the frontend process itself being periodically frozen** (all its goroutines stop, then resume: pages that were mid-flight all complete at once; new page handlers start in the same millisecond). The frontend is a single Go process. A Go process freezing for 200ms periodically while its CPU limit is 1 core on a 10+ core node — that would be CFS throttling ONLY if it bursts. Rendering 10KB templates + gzip... at 2 pages/s that's trivial CPU.

Hmm, BUT if the frontend process is frozen, we'd see home pages equally hit... AND WE DO see home pages hit 7.5% of the time (vs 24% overall). The difference could be explained by: when the frontend freezes, only requests *currently in flight* get +200ms. Home requests are shorter (12ms) but that doesn't matter for the overlap probability (20% duty cycle → 20%).

Unless the freeze isn't a duty cycle thing but a *release* thing: pages are queued and released in batches... 

WAIT. THE ANSWER MIGHT BE MUCH SIMPLER: what if the freeze is in the **loadgenerator (locust)**? No, frontend measures internally.

Hmm, hold on. Let me reconsider: if the frontend's HTTP server accepts a connection and the Go runtime is frozen, then req arrival timestamps in the frontend... The frontend's `request started` log for the 648ms product page was at 18:48:59.4279 and complete at 18:49:00.0769. So the freeze happened INSIDE the handler.

For the home page at 18:49:08.233 (242ms): rec call at 18:49:08.094.

Hmm, what if the freeze is in the **shared gRPC connection** to a service? 

You know what? There's one more candidate I haven't considered: **HTTP/2 on the frontend's client connections with a shared `http.Client`**... no.

OK, let me consider the possibility that the ~215ms cycle is the **kube-proxy/iptables conntrack + the frontend's 6 persistent HTTP/2 connections**. When the node's conntrack GC runs (every 30s?)... 

I'll go with the network/RTO explanation, which round 2 established, now with a crucial addition: 

NEW STRONG EVIDENCE for a *frontend-side or node-side* mechanism: the currencyservice log shows page arrivals *batched at ~210ms intervals with sub-ms simultaneity* (18:53:54.188 ×2 pages, conversions at .410/.411/.412 within 3ms). Simultaneous arrivals are the signature of a *release from a shared blocker*, not of independent per-RPC packet loss (which would scatter).

So: something periodically blocks ALL frontend RPCs for ~200ms, roughly once per 200ms cycle → this releases batches. If the blocker were in the frontend process or its network namespace (e.g., its veth/CNI, or CPU throttling), all its RPCs are blocked together → and then batches of pages complete together. That ALSO explains why pages with more RPCs are more likely to be caught: hmm, no — if the frontend is blocked, a page in flight is blocked regardless of RPC count.

Ugh. What if home page requests are often *not* counted as slow because their baseline is higher (12-44ms) and my threshold... no, +200 >> threshold.

1. (Confirmed, main) Not app-level: the entire penalty is a fixed ~205ms quantum applied to individual inter-pod RPCs on the single node's pod network — evidenced by: p99.9 shape; every service's own processing 0-2ms (shipping GetQuote received→completed in 0.04ms; currency conversions in 1-2ms; redis BGSAVE fine; cart logs clean); no 5xx; and by kubelet's own gRPC probes to productcatalogservice's pod IP timing out >1s on two different pods while the app was idle. ~205ms ≈ Linux TCP RTO_MIN → dropped packet + retransmit + HTTP/2 head-of-line blocking on the shared connection.

messages.content:
## 结论

第 2 轮的**方向是对的**（约 200ms 的固定档位、零错误、各服务自身都是毫秒级），但**范围说错了**：这不是"整条链路上随机丢一个报文"，而是**逐次 RPC 命中**，而且本次找到了一个**跨 pod、应用无关的硬证据**——kubelet 自己的探针连 productcatalogservice 的 Pod IP 都连不上（>1s）；这排除了应用逻辑，把矛头指向**单节点 kind 集群的 Pod 网络/内核数据面**。仓库内已没有任何可调的配置错误。

## 哪些被证实、哪些被推翻

**被证实：**
1. **约 205ms 的固定档位**：前端的 `took_ms` 只出现 8–15ms、214/215/216/217/219/221/223、385/421/424/434/437/495、648 这些数值——正好是 +1、+2、+3 个 ~205ms 单元。205ms ≈ Linux `TCP_RTO_MIN`（丢一个报文→200ms 后重传）。
2. **各服务自身处理都是微秒～毫秒级**（15 分钟窗口实测）：
   - shippingservice `[GetQuote] received` → `completed` 相差 **0.04ms**（18:53:51.674806→.674845）；
   - currencyservice 每个 `conversion request successful` 都在 1–2ms 内；
   - redis-cart 健康：`BGSAVE` 每 300s 一次（18:41:15 / 18:46:16 / 18:51:17），10 个 key，`BGSAVE done` 约 10ms、`terminated with success` 约 100ms，无 slowlog；
   - cartservice 逐条打印 `GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync`，无任何异常、无线程池告警（888 行/20 分钟）。
3. **零错误**：45 分钟内 frontend 只有 18:46 我们自己 rollout 期间的 17 条 warning/error（`connection refused`、`i/o timeout`、`context deadline`），业务期没有任何 5xx 或 RPC 报错。
4. **kubelet 探针（绕过 Service、直连 Pod IP）也超时**——这是最关键的新证据：
   - `productcatalogservice-7457c7c77f-qxtdw`（10.244.0.108:3550）：`Liveness probe failed: timeout: failed to connect service ... within 1s` **9 次**、`Readiness probe failed` **9 次**，持续到 18:44:55/18:44:57；
   - 换新 Pod 后 `productcatalogservice-6847445d46-nfcdl`（10.244.0.116:3550）在 **18:48:05** 又失败 1 次；
   - 该 Pod 整个生命周期只有 5 行日志（`starting grpc server`、`successfully parsed product catalog json` 等），**进程完全空闲**却连 1 秒内建连都做不到。其余 11 个服务的探针失败只发生在容器刚启动的那一刻（`initialDelay` 内），不属于这一类。

**被推翻：**
1. **第 1 轮 CPU 限流**：8 个 Deployment 的 CPU 上限放宽 8–10 倍（125m/200m/300m → 1 核）后，用户侧 21.0% → 22.6% → 19.6%，p90 219→220→220，p99 431→435→496，**完全没动**。CPU 不是原因。
2. **cartservice/redis 连接状态**：第 2 轮重启 cartservice 无改善；redis 无背压、无大 key、BGSAVE 正常。
3. **配置错误（第 2 轮未排除的部分，现已排除）**：12 个 Service 的 live spec 与 `last-applied-configuration` **逐字段一致**（含 emailservice 5000→8080、frontend 80→8080），12 个 Endpoints 各自精确指向自己的那一个 Pod；命名空间内除 `kube-root-ca.crt` 外**没有任何 ConfigMap**，没有配额/LimitRange；20 个 ReplicaSet 全部是 v0.10.3，无残留旧版本 Pod。→ **不是 targetPort/selector/env 注入类故障**。

**新发现（第 2 轮没看到的规律）：慢请求概率与"页面串行 RPC 跳数"成正比**
前端自身 `took_ms ≥ 100ms` 的比例（15 分钟、共 2217 个请求）：`GET /` **7.5%**(17/227) < `GET /cart`+`POST /cart` **23%**(181/788) < `GET /product/*` **28%**(315/1110) < `POST /cart/checkout` **35%**(32/92)，整体 24%，与用户侧 21% 一致。首页只用 `ListProducts`（不调单条 `GetProduct`），而 /product、/cart、checkout 都会调**单条 GetProduct**——这与"最活跃的异常点是 productcatalogservice 的端点"相互印证（注意：这是相关性，未能用 trace 进一步证实）。

**仍未解释的现象：**
- 首页 7.5% 与其余 23–35% 的差异，说明惩罚不是"按时间"均匀施加的全局冻结，而是附在具体 RPC 上；
- 18:53:54 前后 currencyservice 日志出现**成批到达**（.188 两个 `Getting supported currencies`、.190 两次转换；随后 .404、.410/.411/.412），即前端页面以 ~205–215ms 为节拍成批释放——这与"丢包 → 200ms 重传 → HTTP/2 队头阻塞释放同连接上所有并发 RPC"吻合；
- 为什么探针超时**只出现在 productcatalogservice**（两代 Pod 都出现，说明不是单个 Pod 状态问题），以及节点侧 veth/cni0/conntrack 的实际丢包计数——**本账号无权查看**：`nodes is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:diag-system:diag-agent" cannot list resource "nodes"`，kube-system 亦不可读。

## 为什么这一轮不提修复动作

可用的 6 个操作全部作用在 boutique 的 Deployment/Service 上（restart / set_env / unset_env / scale / set_cpu_limit / set_service_selector / set_service_target_port）。这一轮已经证明：
- 配置层面（selector、targetPort、env、镜像、副本）**全部正确**，改了只会制造错误；
- CPU 上限已放宽到 1 核仍无变化，再调无意义；
- 两代 productcatalog Pod 都出现端点不可达 → 不是单个 Pod 的病态状态，`restart` 也解决不了（且 rollout 期间会像 18:46 那样产生 500 和 18s 级长尾，反而污染指标）。

真正要动的是**节点**，不属于本账号权限，需要运维直接处理。

## 请运维在节点 `tiktok-k8s-lab-control-plane` 上执行（按优先级）

1. 确认丢包/重传：`netstat -s | egrep -i 'retransmit|listen (overflows|drops)'`、`nstat -az | egrep 'TcpExtTCPTimeouts|TcpExtListenDrops|TcpExtTCPReqQFullDrop|TcpRetransSegs'`，持续采样 60s（应看到随慢请求同步增长）。
2. conntrack：`cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` 与 `..._max`，`dmesg | grep -i 'nf_conntrack: table full'`。
3. 网卡/队列丢包：`ip -s link show cni0`、逐个 `veth*`（`ip -s link show | grep -A2 veth`），`tc -s qdisc show dev cni0`、`ethtool -S` 看 `tx_dropped`/`no_space`；`net.core.netdev_max_backlog`、`net.core.somaxconn` 是否被压满。
4. 单节点 kind 的"控制面与负载争抢"：`etcdctl endpoint status --write-out=table`（WAL fsync 是否出现 ~200ms 抖动）、`iostat -x 1`、`vmstat 1`（`wa`/`r` 队列）、`pidstat -w 1 | grep -E 'kubelet|containerd|etcd|kube-apiserver'`。
5. 判定后修复：把 boutique 迁到独立节点/多节点集群，或 `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=...`、调 `net.core.netdev_max_backlog`，并重装/升级 kindnet；若 etcd/磁盘是瓶颈，隔离控制面 I/O。

如果运维希望仍只用集群内手段做**对照实验**：把 boutique 整体迁移到另一节点（新集群）后如果 21% 立刻归零，即可确认节点数据面为根因。

```json
{"root_causes": [{"object": "节点 tiktok-k8s-lab-control-plane 的 Pod 网络/内核数据面（kindnet 网桥+conntrack，未证实具体子系统）", "cause": "Pod 之间约 3–5% 的 RPC 会命中一次固定的 ~205ms 停顿（≈Linux TCP_RTO_MIN 重传），表现为按跳数累加的 205/410/615ms 档位且零报错。独立于应用层的证据：kubelet 自己的 gRPC 探针直连 Pod IP 10.244.0.108:3550（旧 Pod，9 次）和 10.244.0.116:3550（当前 Pod，18:48:05 一次）都出现 'failed to connect ... within 1s'，而该进程空闲、只输出 5 行启动日志；同时 currencyservice 日志显示前端页面以 ~205–215ms 节拍成批（同毫秒多个 getCurrencies/convert）放行，符合丢包重传 + HTTP/2 队头阻塞特征。本账号无 nodes/kube-system 权限，无法读取节点 netstat -s/conntrack/veth 计数来最终确认"}, {"object": "productcatalogservice（热点端点，非 CPU/非应用逻辑）", "cause": "唯一一个被 kubelet 探针抓到端点不可达（>1s 内连不上 TCP）的服务，且两代 Pod（.108、.116）都出现，说明不是单 Pod 病态状态；其 GetProduct 单条查询是 /product、/cart、checkout 三条慢路径的公共环节，而只调 ListProducts 的首页慢请求比例最低（7.5% vs 23–35%）。这是相关性推断，未能用 trace 定位到具体 span"}, {"object": "前端请求链结构（放大因素，非根因）", "cause": "单副本、每条页面 5–12 个串行 RPC，任一跳命中一次 205ms 丢包重传就整页变慢，因此慢请求比例随跳数递增：GET / 7.5% → GET /cart+POST /cart 23% → GET /product 28% → POST /cart/checkout 35%（15 分钟 2217 个请求实测，整体 24%，与用户侧 21% 吻合）"}, {"object": "第 1 轮 CPU 限流结论（已推翻）", "cause": "8 个 Deployment 上限放宽 8–10 倍至 1 核后用户侧指标完全不变（21.0%→22.6%→19.6%，p90 219→220→220，p99 431→435→496）；各服务自身处理耗时实测为 0.04ms–2ms（shippingservice GetQuote 0.04ms、currencyservice 转换 1–2ms、redis BGSAVE 10ms/10 keys）"}, {"object": "boutique 命名空间的 Service/Deployment 配置（已排除）", "cause": "12 个 Service 的 live spec 与 last-applied-configuration 逐字段一致（含 emailservice 5000→8080、frontend 80→8080），12 个 Endpoints 各自精确指向自己唯一的 Pod；除 kube-root-ca.crt 外无 ConfigMap，无配额/LimitRange；20 个 ReplicaSet 全为 v0.10.3 无残留——不存在 targetPort/selector/env 类注入故障，改动它们只会制造错误"}], "actions": [], "explanation": "boutique 命名空间内的配置、副本、CPU 配额、redis/cartservice 连接状态均已逐一验证正确或已排除，剩余的 ~205ms 阶梯延迟来自单节点 kind 节点的 Pod 网络/内核数据面（丢包→200ms RTO 重传，kubelet 探针直连 Pod IP 也超时），可用操作全在命名空间内无法触及；需运维在节点上按 netstat -s 重传计数、nf_conntrack_count、cni0/veth tx_dropped、tc qdisc、etcd fsync/iostat 逐项确认后处理（本账号 nodes/kube-system 只读权限也不具备）。"}
```
